definition: Pervious concrete (also called porous concrete, permeable concrete, no fines concrete and porous pavement) is a special type of [concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete) with a high [porosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porosity) used for concrete [flatwork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete_slab) applications that allows [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) from [precipitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology)) and other sources to pass directly through, thereby reducing the [runoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_runoff) from a site and allowing [groundwater recharge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groundwater_recharge).

Pesticide application is the practical way in which [pesticide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesticide)s (including [herbicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbicide)s, [fungicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungicide)s, [insecticide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insecticide)s, or [nematicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematicide)s) are delivered to their biological targets (e.g. [pest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest_(organism)) organism, [crop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crop) or other plant).
Pesticide drift, also known as spray drift, is the unintentional diffusion of [pesticide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesticide)s toward nontarget species.
Pesticide residue refers to the [pesticide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesticide)s that may remain on or in food, after they are applied to [food crop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_crop)s.
